tasks.residual_work: Must construct a concrete failing input by reasoning about the buggy update l = m (non-progress when a[m] < t and m == l) and the r = len(a)-1 convention that cannot return len(a). No counterexample is supplied.

minimum_answer: Counterexample: a = [1, 3], t = 2. Initially l=0, r=1, m=0; a[0]=1<2 so l=m=0, and l<r still holds with m=0 again, so the loop never terminates (or, for a=[5], t=1, it returns 0 instead of len(a)). Repair using half-open interval [l, r): l=0, r=len(a); while l<r: m=(l+r)//2; if a[m]<t: l=m+1 else: r=m; return l. Termination: each iteration either sets l=m+1>l or r=m<r, strictly shrinking r-l, so the loop ends. Boundary: maintain invariant that all indices <l have a[i]<t and all indices >=r have a[i]>=t; on exit l==r, so l is the smallest index with a[i]>=t, or len(a) if none. Duplicates are handled because r=m keeps the leftmost qualifying index; t above all entries drives l to len(a).
